analysis: The only change in EngineV2SlotFactory.swift is one added argument, `stopStringScope: ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope(modelId:modelType:)`, in the `EngineV2Factory.makeBridge` call (head line 574). It uses the same modelId and modelType inputs as the existing `effectiveEOSTokenIds` call. The change adds no new inputs from consumers or providers, and it does not touch the authorization, attestation, encryption or prefix-cache paths in this file. Those paths include SSD cache construction, weightHash and promptContractID binding, cacheSalt plumbing and KV budget reservation, all of which are unchanged (T-041). This is a stop-string handling scope that affects output termination, a generation-behavior policy. It has no direct bearing on A-001 confidentiality, keys, or the TB-002 wire contract. The visible effect is on availability and correctness: a wrongly scoped stop string could truncate output early or leave generation running longer (T-010, T-029). I saw no evidence of either. Not visible in the supplied evidence: the `ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope` implementation, the `makeBridge` signature and default (its parameter-ordering compatibility), and how the bridge consumes the scope when matching stop strings against decoded text or prompt content. I treat these as an unverified contract and not as a finding. A reviewer of the other changed files in this PR should confirm that stop-string matching neither leaks content across requests nor allows consumer-controlled unbounded stop strings to cause DoS. No regression is identified in this file.
